method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5) 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)' (published 15 August and 5 September 2016), 22 claims; LICENCE: © 2016 AMPCo Pty Ltd. All rights reserved (read at the copyright line of each article PDF (free-to-read PDFs linked from the MJA article pages)). S2: QUOTED from European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062) 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research' (published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026)), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC12670475). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research position statement on cardiovascular safety after TRAVERSE (Andrology, CC BY 4.0, quoted), for post-2016 cardiovascular evidence and practical monitoring. S2 says it is not written as a guideline, and its meeting and publication were funded by Androlabs (stated in its acknowledgments). S1 claims and anchors are unchanged.

claims.claim: **Pathological hypogonadism comes from disease of the hypothalamus or pituitary (hypogonadotropic) or of the testes (hypergonadotropic).** It is diagnosed clinically, rests on a pathological cause, and is confirmed with hormone tests.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary testicular failure, with raised LH and FSH, is the most common form;** failure of hypothalamic–pituitary drive, before or after puberty, is less common.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a full history:** smoking, medicines, alcohol and other drugs (above all androgens), undescended testes or genital anomalies, puberty, past fertility, erections, libido, and pelvic surgery, genital trauma or infection. **Examine** height, weight (waist if obese), gynaecomastia, virilisation and testicular volume with an orchidometer.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Klinefelter syndrome, about one in 580 males, is missed in more than half of affected men,** often because nobody examines the genitals; the small testes give it away.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test only when the clinical picture suggests pathological androgen deficiency, never as population screening.** Measure total testosterone with LH and FSH early in the morning (08:00 to 10:00); shift workers or the sleep-deprived can be tested soon after waking.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mass spectrometry assays are preferred where available;** immunoassays are non-specific and method-biased.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Always repeat a low result:** up to 30% of men with one low testosterone are normal on retesting. Unless the first set is clearly diagnostic, base the diagnosis on at least two measurements of testosterone, LH and FSH.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Interpret against SHBG:** it rises with hyperthyroidism, liver disease and antiepileptic drugs, and falls with obesity, insulin resistance and exogenous androgens. A low testosterone with low SHBG and normal LH and FSH does not prove deficiency. **Calculated free testosterone should not guide decisions.**
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected hypogonadotropic hypogonadism needs further tests** for treatable causes: prolactin, iron studies and full blood count, anterior pituitary function, and pituitary MRI when pituitary or hypothalamic disease is suspected.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start testosterone before the work-up is finished and a definite pathological cause is found:** it can hide a pituitary tumour, suppresses the axis so later assessment is hard, commits the man to lifelong treatment, and harms fertility, whereas gonadotropins can restore sperm production in secondary hypogonadism.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Men with pathological hypogonadism should receive testosterone replacement at any age.** Age alone neither justifies nor rules out treatment; in very old men with comorbidities weigh benefit against risk, and start slowly and carefully.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Without hypothalamic, pituitary or testicular disease, testosterone is not justified in older men with comorbidities.** Their low testosterone marks poor general health: manage the underlying illness or depression first, and seek endocrinology review if the diagnosis is uncertain.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In obesity, low testosterone with normal LH and FSH mostly reflects reversible axis suppression.** Encourage weight loss by diet and exercise (10% weight loss raises testosterone measurably); if testosterone stays low after successful weight loss, reassess for a missed pathological cause.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In metabolic syndrome or diabetes, testosterone gave only a marginal change in insulin sensitivity and no better glucose control;** prioritise lifestyle change, weight loss and glycaemic control.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Glucocorticoids and opioids lower testosterone, possibly reversibly.** Withdraw them where possible; if they must continue, an endocrinologist can review the balance of options.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S2 position (differs from S1):** confirm hypogonadism with consistent symptoms and a low testosterone (EAU and EAA use 12.0 nmol/L as the cut-off), and separate organic (primary or secondary) from functional hypogonadism. In functional hypogonadism, weight management and physical activity come first and must precede testosterone; S2 then treats testosterone as an option, whereas S1 does not justify it without a pathological cause.
claims.source_text: Accurate diagnosis: Confirm hypogonadism with consistent symptoms (e.g., fatigue, low libido) and low serum testosterone according to guidelines. The EAU and EAA guidelines mention 12.0 nmol/L as cut‐off. … A distinction between functional and organic hypogonadism for individualized treatment is required. The latter forms can be primary or secondary hypogonadism. This "classical form" of hypogonadism can be of testicular origin or due to hypothalamic-pituitary failure, thus have definitive etiologies. Functional hypogonadism represents a clinical condition associated with comorbidities (e.g., obesity, MetS), which can act either at central or peripheral level, potentially requiring lifestyle intervention prior to TTh. … Especially in functional hypogonadism, where the underlying morbidity is most often obesity‐associated, this is a paramount key to success of treatment and must precede TTh.
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start testosterone** when paternity is wanted, with unexplained prostate or breast changes, or with a high haematocrit; avoid it with untreated sleep apnoea, severe heart failure, a recent cardiovascular event or hormone-sensitive cancer unless a specialist is guiding care. (S2)
claims.source_text: TTh should not be initiated in case of desired paternity, unclear processes of the prostate, mammary gland, or high hematocrit (Hct) level. … Exclude contraindications: Avoid TTh in men with untreated sleep apnea, severe heart failure, a recent CV event, or hormone‐sensitive cancers unless under specialist guidance.
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Replace with testosterone itself.** Depot intramuscular injection and transdermal gel, cream or liquid are convenient and cost-effective; aim to relieve symptoms and signs at standard doses, keeping levels within the eugonadal reference interval.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Judge efficacy by the man's leading symptom and by trough levels** (sampled just before the next dose) for injectable or transdermal products, aiming for the lower part of the eugonadal range. Random samples mean nothing, and oral testosterone cannot be monitored this way. Persistently raised LH in primary testicular failure suggests under-dosing or poor adherence; periodic bone density helps too.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check haemoglobin or haematocrit 3 months after starting, then yearly;** a rise above normal is more likely in smokers. If polycythaemia develops, look for smoking, sleep apnoea or respiratory failure and lower the dose or frequency; venesection is rarely needed.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prostate:** there is no convincing excess risk in treated hypogonadal men, so monitor as for eugonadal men of the same age. But if substantive prostate disease is reasonably possible, do a digital rectal exam and PSA before starting. Routine PSA monitoring can turn into screening, with overdiagnosis.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cardiovascular evidence is conflicting:** until better data exist, be cautious with testosterone in older men who have established heart or vascular disease, above all those without pathological hypogonadism.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Injections are relatively contraindicated with bleeding disorders or anticoagulants** (haematoma risk), so prefer a transdermal product; all injections can cause pain, bruising and a cough from oil microembolism. **Apply transdermal products after the morning shower and cover them** to avoid transfer to children or partners.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Obstructive sleep apnoea is not an absolute bar:** testosterone worsens it only briefly, unless it is severe and untreated.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When to sample testosterone (S2):** on gel, about 2–4 h after the last application; on long-acting testosterone undecanoate, preferably 1 week before the next injection (delay the injection if the level is still high-normal); on short-acting injections, just before the next dose. Titrate gels by daily dose and injections by the interval.
claims.source_text: Gel formulations: Measure trough levels ∼2-4 h after the last application. ✓ Injectables: Timing depends on the formulation. For long‐acting T undecanoate, measure preferably 1 week before the next injection (the next injection might be adjourned in case of levels still being within the higher normal range). For short acting injections, measure directly before the next injection. … Dosing: Transdermal Gel preparations can be easily titrated in daily dose, injectable forms of treatment should be titrated by modulating injection intervals
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Haematocrit (S2 schedule): every 3–6 months in the first year, then yearly, keeping it below 54%.** If it rises too high, lower the dose, change formulation or pause treatment; phlebotomy may be needed. S1's schedule is at 3 months, then yearly.
claims.source_text: Check Hct every 3-6 months in the first year, then annually, keeping levels below 54% to minimize thromboembolic risk. … Erythrocytosis: If Hct exceeds safe limits, adjust TTh dosage, consider a different formulation, or temporarily stop therapy. Phlebotomy may be warranted to reduce Hct.
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: 🇦🇺 **Australian T4DM trial:** 22% of men on testosterone undecanoate injections had a haematocrit above 0.52 on fasting samples taken in a hot climate, but only 2.5% on repeat non-fasting samples.
claims.source_text: In the Australian T4DM study, during which more than 1000 men received intramuscular injections of T undecanoate versus placebo, 22% using T had an elevated Hct > 0.52. These blood samples were taken under fasting conditions in a hot country. On repeat samples in a non‐fasting condition the incidence of an elevated Hct fell to 2.5%.
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **PSA usually rises on testosterone:** a rise of up to 1.4 ng/mL a year is generally considered safe; more than that needs urological evaluation. Monitor lower urinary tract symptoms. (S2)
claims.source_text: Prostate health surveillance: Monitor PSA levels and perform prostate exams. PSA levels are likely to increase with TTh. PSA increases ≤1.4 ng/mL/year are generally considered safe. Increases beyond this threshold warrant urologic evaluation. Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) require regular monitoring.
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **TRAVERSE (5246 men aged 45–80 with functional hypogonadism, most with cardiovascular disease or high risk) found no significant increase in major adverse cardiovascular events** on 1.62% testosterone gel titrated to 350–750 ng/dL for a mean of 22 months. Heart failure and cardiovascular death did not differ.
claims.source_text: TRAVERSE enrolled 5246, 45-80‐year‐old men (mean age 63.3 years; 47% older than 65 years of age) with functional hypogonadism as above mentioned. Most suffered from existing CV disease or they were at high risk of CV events. Mean body mass index was 35 kg m-2. Approximately 70% had T2DM (HbA1c 6.5-11%), and 90% had hypertension and dyslipidemia. Participants received either placebo or T gel (a 1.62% gel), titrated to maintain physiological serum T levels (350-750 ng/dL) for a mean of 22 months. … Results showed no statistically significant increase in CV risk in the TTh group compared with placebo when either primary or secondary end points were considered. … No significant differences were seen in CV death or heart failure.
claims.locator: European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research (PaTeR) (Zitzmann M, Rastrelli G, Murray RD, et al.), Andrology 2026;14:294-302 (doi 10.1111/andr.70062), 'Cardiovascular safety of testosterone therapy - Insights from the TRAVERSE trial and beyond: A position statement of the European Expert Panel for Testosterone Research', published online 15 May 2025 (issue 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12670475/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **But atrial fibrillation and non-fatal arrhythmias rose slightly but significantly,** and the trial's limits matter: an older, high-risk group (mean age 63.3, BMI 35, about 70% with T2DM), follow-up of only about 22 months, and too few events to settle arrhythmia and heart failure.
claims.source_text: While there was a minor, but significant, increase in AF and non‐fatal arrhythmias … TRAVERSE included an older, high‐risk population (mean age 63.3 years, BMI 35, ∼70% with T2DM), limiting generalizability to younger, healthier hypogonadal men. In these men, CV events may seem less likely, but it is also possible that monitoring is less strict Exclusion of men with low baseline CV risk makes the findings less applicable to this subgroup. The study does not address long‐term CV outcomes beyond ∼22 months. Endpoints like arrhythmias and heart failure were underpowered for definitive conclusions.
